```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_ade4 <- requireNamespace("ade4", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(canofac)
```

## Data and preprocessing

The Friday (1987) data (package **ade4**) describe 16 ponds by the abundance
of 91 species in 10 blocks (taxonomic groups). Each block is centred by column and
brought to unit total inertia, the default normalisation of the package.

```{r, eval = has_ade4}
blocks <- cf_friday()
sapply(blocks, ncol)
```

## The q-family

`q = 2` with unconstrained axes is CPCA; `q = 4` with simultaneous extraction
is INDORT, and with sequential extraction ACCPS (CCSWA, ComDim).

```{r, eval = has_ade4}
fit2 <- canofac(blocks, R = 2, q = 2)
fit4 <- canofac(blocks, R = 2, q = 4)
fit4
```

The saliences `fit4$saliences` are the shares of the inertia of each block
carried by each reference component.

## Trajectories

```{r, eval = has_ade4, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
tr <- cf_trajectories(blocks, R = 2, qgrid = c(1, 1.5, 1.9, 2, 2.1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10))
plot(tr)
```

## Plots of a fit

```{r, eval = has_ade4, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
plot(fit4, labels = TRUE)          # individuals on the reference components
plot(fit4, type = "saliences")     # saliences per block and dimension
```

## Permutation test

```{r, eval = has_ade4}
test <- cf_test(blocks, R = 2, q = 2, B = 199, seed = 1)
test
plot(test)
```

For each block, the test estimates the reference components of the other
blocks, `U^(-k)`, and compares the link between the block and these components
with the links obtained after permuting the rows of the block: the LOBO
(leave-one-block-out) test. **All the blocks** are linked to the subspace when its p-value is
below `alpha` for every block. Otherwise, the blocks linked to it are those
whose Holm-adjusted p-value is below `alpha`: several, one or none. The
p-values of each component of the other blocks are descriptive; a component
is linked when at least one block is linked to it after Holm adjustment.
Being linked is not a label: a component may mix directions that the blocks
carry differently, and a block may be linked to it through a small share
only. Labeling parts of the retained space as common, shared, private or
residual is done by CoPRes (<https://github.com/hanafisoft/CoPRes>). The
previous statistic, which re-estimates the whole model on each permuted data
set, is available with `statistic = "refit"`; it loses its power for a second
link and is used only as a global test.

Further options of `cf_test()`: `pvalue = "hybrid"` (gamma approximation with
the exact permutation moments, permutation only near the thresholds),
`scheme = "groups"` with `groups` (replicates), `compare = TRUE` (full RV test
and PROTEST, as comparisons), and `plot(test, type = "null")` (permutation
distributions). With the same `seed`, the Python version of canofac gives the
same p-values.

## Choice of the number of dimensions (experimental)

`cf_test_path()` is **experimental**: the choice of R is not part of the
published articles, and the p-values of the chosen model are optimistic. A
warning is issued at each call.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pth <- cf_test_path(blocks, q = 2, B = 199, seed = 1)  # models r = 1, ..., K + 2
pth
plot(pth)
```

For q > 2 the criterion can be multimodal: `canofac()` and `cf_test()` use 10
starts by default (argument `nstart`).

## Graphics module and language of the results

The functions `cf_plot_scores()`, `cf_plot_saliences()`,
`cf_plot_trajectories()`, `cf_plot_test()` and `cf_plot_compare()` draw the
main results; the `plot()` methods call them. The labels of the printed and
plotted results are in English by default; `cf_lang("fr")` switches them to
French. The values stored in the objects (for example `test$link`) do not
depend on the language.

```{r, eval = has_ade4, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
cf_plot_saliences(fit4)
fits <- list("q = 1" = canofac(blocks, R = 2, q = 1), CPCA = fit2, INDORT = fit4)
cf_plot_compare(fits, dim = 1)
old <- cf_lang("fr")
cf_plot_test(test)
cf_lang(old)
```

Help in French: `cf_help("cf_test", "fr")`; a French version of this vignette
is available (`vignette("canofac-fr", package = "canofac")`). A complete
commented script, in French, runs the whole analysis step by step:
`system.file("scripts", "canofac_step_by_step.R", package = "canofac")`.
